status: exact delta-localized positive-boundary reduction and endpoint-uniformity route guard; the compact strip family remains open and this is not a proof of Lambda<=0 or RH
proof_boundary: The gate proves a logical localization and an exact quadratic countermodel only. It does not certify any new Xi compact rectangle, positive-time simplicity, Lambda<=0, or RH.

exact.boundary_attainment: If Lambda>0, then 0<Lambda<=1/5 and H_Lambda has a finite real multiple zero
exact.positive_time_equivalence: Lambda<=0 iff H_t has only simple zeros for every 0<t<=1/5
exact.delta_contradiction: To contradict Lambda>0 it is enough, for every rational delta in (0,1/5], to exclude common zeros of H_t and H_t' on delta<=t<=1/5; choose any rational delta<Lambda
exact.dominant_localization: For fixed delta>0, t>=delta and L=log(|x|/(4*pi))>=25/delta imply tL>=25 and L>=50, so the dominant-saddle theorem gives H_t'(x)^2-H_t(x)H_t''(x)>0
exact.compact_rectangle: Every multiple zero with delta<=t<=1/5 lies in |x|<R_delta, R_delta=4*pi*exp(25/delta)
exact.cofinal_sequence: For delta_j=1/(5j), j>=1, Lambda<=0 iff (H_t,H_t')!=(0,0) on [delta_j,1/5]x[-4*pi*exp(125j),4*pi*exp(125j)] for every j
exact.compact_minimum: For each fixed j, no common zero on the compact rectangle is equivalent to min(H_t(x)^2+H_t'(x)^2)>0 there
exact.corrected_delta_target: A sufficient nonuniform route is: for each fixed delta>0, prove the corrected C1 finite-main inequality only on delta<=t<=1/5 and 38<|x|<4*pi*exp(25/delta), with constants allowed to deteriorate as delta decreases
exact.quadratic_model: G_t(x)=x^2-2t solves partial_t G=-partial_x^2 G; for t>0 it has the simple real zeros +/-sqrt(2t), at t=0 it has a double zero, and for t<0 its zeros are nonreal
exact.quadratic_margins: L[G_t]=G_t'^2-G_t G_t''=2x^2+4t>0 for t>0, while G_t(0)^2+(G_t'(0)/A)^2=4t^2 and at either root the same first-jet quantity is 8t/A^2; both margins tend to zero as t decreases to zero
exact.route_reclassification: A t-independent positive first-jet floor down to t=0 is a valid stronger sufficient target, but it is not logically necessary for Lambda<=0 or positive-time simplicity
exact.proof_handoff: Use delta-dependent compact or arithmetic transversality estimates, or keep the uniform scaled small-ball theorem as an optional stronger route; do not require endpoint simplicity without stating that extra burden

rows.claim: A hypothetical positive Newman boundary is attained at a finite real multiple zero.

rows.proof_boundary: Uses the separately validated Polymath-15 compactness handoff.

rows.claim: The Newman direction is exactly a positive-time simplicity problem.
rows.formula: Lambda<=0 iff H_t has only simple zeros for every 0<t<=1/5
rows.proof_boundary: Uses the published bound Lambda<=1/5 and simplicity above Lambda.

rows.claim: Uniformity as t tends to zero is not needed in the contradiction argument.

rows.proof_boundary: The family must hold for a cofinal set of positive deltas.

rows.claim: For each fixed positive lower time, the dominant-saddle theorem makes the remaining frequency range compact.
rows.formula: For fixed delta>0, t>=delta and L=log(|x|/(4*pi))>=25/delta imply tL>=25 and L>=50, so the dominant-saddle theorem gives H_t'(x)^2-H_t(x)H_t''(x)>0; Every multiple zero with delta<=t<=1/5 lies in |x|<R_delta, R_delta=4*pi*exp(25/delta)
rows.proof_boundary: The compact radius grows exponentially as delta decreases.

rows.claim: One explicit countable sequence of compact strips is equivalent to the Newman direction.
rows.formula: For delta_j=1/(5j), j>=1, Lambda<=0 iff (H_t,H_t')!=(0,0) on [delta_j,1/5]x[-4*pi*exp(125j),4*pi*exp(125j)] for every j
rows.proof_boundary: This is a logical equivalence, not a certificate for any strip.

rows.claim: Each fixed strip has an ordinary compact nonvanishing formulation.
rows.formula: For each fixed j, no common zero on the compact rectangle is equivalent to min(H_t(x)^2+H_t'(x)^2)>0 there
rows.proof_boundary: No effective positive minimum is supplied.

rows.claim: A delta-dependent corrected first-jet certificate would suffice without endpoint-uniform margins.
rows.formula: A sufficient nonuniform route is: for each fixed delta>0, prove the corrected C1 finite-main inequality only on delta<=t<=1/5 and 38<|x|<4*pi*exp(25/delta), with constants allowed to deteriorate as delta decreases
rows.proof_boundary: Open for every cofinal delta; the displayed radii are far beyond current compact certificates.

rows.claim: The backward heat equation permits Lambda=0 with positive-time simplicity and a double endpoint zero.
rows.formula: G_t(x)=x^2-2t solves partial_t G=-partial_x^2 G; for t>0 it has the simple real zeros +/-sqrt(2t), at t=0 it has a double zero, and for t<0 its zeros are nonreal
rows.proof_boundary: Generic heat-flow calibration, not a model of Xi arithmetic.

rows.claim: A positive first-jet floor uniform down to t=0 is stronger than the required positive-time simplicity statement.
rows.formula: L[G_t]=G_t'^2-G_t G_t''=2x^2+4t>0 for t>0, while G_t(0)^2+(G_t'(0)/A)^2=4t^2 and at either root the same first-jet quantity is 8t/A^2; both margins tend to zero as t decreases to zero; A t-independent positive first-jet floor down to t=0 is a valid stronger sufficient target, but it is not logically necessary for Lambda<=0 or positive-time simplicity
rows.proof_boundary: Does not show that a stronger Xi-specific uniform theorem is false.
